CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Cancer Center
Department of Hematopathology and Molecular Diagnostics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Specimen Type: Bone Marrow Aspirate
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL DETAILS
Clinical Indication: Suspected myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS)
Referring Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Department: Hematology/Oncology

METHODOLOGY

Conventional Cytogenetics:
G-banded chromosome analysis was attempted on cultured bone marrow cells using standard techniques. Twenty metaphases were targeted for analysis at 400-550 band resolution.

Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization (FISH):
Interphase FISH analysis was performed using the following dual-color probe sets:
- EGR1/D5S23,D5S721 Dual Color Probe Set (Abbott Molecular)
  EGR1 (5q31): SpectrumOrange
  D5S23,D5S721 (5p15.2): SpectrumGreen
- D7S486/CEP7 Dual Color Probe Set (Abbott Molecular)
  D7S486 (7q31): SpectrumOrange
  CEP7 (centromere 7): SpectrumGreen

One hundred interphase nuclei were analyzed for each probe set according to laboratory guidelines.

RESULTS

Conventional Cytogenetics:
Analysis failed due to insufficient dividing cells. The specimen was received 4 days post-collection, which likely contributed to poor cell viability and proliferation in culture.

FISH Analysis:
EGR1 (5q31) deletion: NOT DETECTED
- 100/100 cells showed two EGR1 signals and two 5p15.2 signals
- Normal signal pattern: 2O2G

D7S486 (7q31) deletion: NOT DETECTED
- 100/100 cells showed two D7S486 signals and two CEP7 signals
- Normal signal pattern: 2O2G

INTERPRETATION
G-banded cytogenetic analysis could not be completed due to culture failure related to specimen age and insufficient mitotic cells. FISH analysis using probes targeting the commonly deleted regions in MDS (5q31 and 7q31) showed no evidence of deletion in the cells examined. These results indicate:

1. No deletion of the EGR1 gene region at 5q31
2. No deletion of chromosome 7q31 region
3. No evidence of monosomy 5 or monosomy 7

While these FISH results are negative for the most common chromosomal abnormalities associated with MDS, they do not exclude the diagnosis. Other cytogenetic abnormalities not covered by this limited FISH panel may be present. Additionally, approximately 40-50% of MDS cases have normal cytogenetics.

CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS
No evidence of common chromosomal abnormalities associated with MDS was detected by FISH analysis. The absence of del(5q) and del(7q) does not rule out MDS, as these abnormalities are present in only a subset of cases. Clinical correlation with morphologic findings, complete blood count parameters, and other diagnostic studies is recommended for definitive diagnosis.

Authorized by: [redacted name], Ph.D., FACMG
Director, Cytogenetics Laboratory
Board Certified Clinical Cytogeneticist
